name: EMDR (Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing)
founders: Francine Shapiro, PhD (1948-2019; PhD 1988, Professional School of Psychological Studies, San Diego, unaccredited and now defunct; later Senior Research Fellow, Mental Research Institute, Palo Alto)
founded_year_range: 1987-1995 (1987: Shapiro's observation; 1989: first published as EMD; 1990: EMDR Institute; 1991: renamed EMDR; 1993: Institute incorporated; 1995: training restrictions lifted, EMDRIA founded; 2014: 'EMDR therapy'), per emdr.com history page
cost_summary: No central price. Therapy sessions (estimate; no official client fee published): US about US$100-250 each, 6-15 sessions typical, so roughly US$1,000-3,000 per course. Clinician training (verified, emdr.com 2026): EMDR Institute basic training is 2 weekends at US$750 each for licensed clinicians (US$685 non-profit/pre-licensed) plus 10 h required consultation (group ~US$30-50/h), about US$1,800-2,000 total. EMDRIA minimum is 20 h instruction + 20 h practicum + 10 h consultation. Free on the NHS for PTSD.
mechanism_summary: Shapiro's Adaptive Information Processing (AIP) model holds that symptoms come from inadequately processed adverse memories, stored with their original images, emotions, body sensations and negative beliefs. Bilateral stimulation during recall is said to engage innate processing that integrates these memories adaptively. Research accounts instead propose working-memory taxing that reduces vividness and leads to reconsolidation, or plain exposure/extinction. For chronic pain, 'pain memories' (pre-amputation pain, injuries, medical trauma) and trauma-linked threat sensitization are proposed to maintain pain. Processing these memories and the current pain sensation is proposed to reduce pain and distress. The model is transdiagnostic in principle, but the pain applications target mainly trauma-exposed or highly distressed patients.
techniques: 8-phase protocol (history, preparation, assessment, desensitization, installation, body scan, closure, re-evaluation)
bilateral stimulation: therapist-guided eye movements, alternating taps, tones, light bar
SUD and VoC ratings; negative/positive cognition
safe/calm place imagery and resource installation
three-pronged targeting of past memories, present triggers and future templates
pain-focused protocols that target the current pain sensation and injury/medical memories
group EMDR for chronic pain (4 days x 5 h)
mainstream_notes: Recommended for PTSD by WHO 2013, NICE NG116 2018, ISTSS 2018 and VA/DoD 2017/2023 (2023: strong recommendation alongside PE and CPT); APA 2017 conditional; Cochrane 2013 includes it with TF-CBT. Delivered in NHS, VA, and Dutch and German routine care. For chronic pain and somatic conditions adoption is limited: German psychosomatic pain centres (EMDR Pain Network Germany) and UK FND trials. Not in chronic pain guidelines such as NICE NG193.
insurance_notes: Reimbursed as standard psychotherapy (US CPT 90834/90837) by commercial insurers, Medicare and Medicaid when a licensed clinician treats a covered diagnosis. There is no EMDR-specific code. Pain-only indications need a coded mental-health diagnosis. Free via the NHS for PTSD.

key_trials.citation: Shapiro F. 1989. Efficacy of the eye movement desensitization procedure in the treatment of traumatic memories. J Trauma Stress 2:199-223
key_trials.design: Randomized controlled study (founding trial; developer-run, unblinded)
key_trials.finding: EMD reduced distress (SUD) from traumatic memories vs an imagery-based (modified flooding) comparison; founding study of EMD

key_trials.citation: Davidson PR, Parker KC. 2001. EMDR: a meta-analysis. J Consult Clin Psychol 69:305-16
key_trials.finding: EMDR beats no treatment but is no better than other exposure techniques; no incremental effect of eye movements

key_trials.citation: Lee CW, Cuijpers P. 2013. A meta-analysis of the contribution of eye movements in processing emotional memories. J Behav Ther Exp Psychiatry 44:231-9
key_trials.finding: Additive eye-movement effect d=0.41 in clinical trials and d=0.74 in lab studies

key_trials.citation: Wright SL et al. 2024. EMDR v. other psychological therapies for PTSD: systematic review and IPD meta-analysis. Psychol Med 54:1580-1588
key_trials.design: Individual participant data meta-analysis (8 of 15 eligible RCTs)
key_trials.finding: No significant difference between EMDR and other psychological therapies on PTSD severity, response, remission or dropout

key_trials.citation: de Roos C et al. 2010. Treatment of chronic phantom limb pain using a trauma-focused psychological approach. Pain Res Manag 15:65-71
key_trials.finding: Significant PLP reduction maintained at 3 months; 3 of 6 pain-free at ~2.8-year follow-up

key_trials.citation: Gerhardt A et al. 2016. EMDR vs treatment-as-usual for non-specific chronic back pain patients with psychological trauma. Front Psychiatry 7:201
key_trials.design: Pilot RCT, 10 sessions pain-focused EMDR + TAU vs TAU
key_trials.finding: Pain intensity d=0.79 post-treatment and 0.50 at 6 months; disability not significant; ~50% clinically improved vs 0 in controls

key_trials.citation: Rostaminejad A et al. 2017. Efficacy of EMDR on the phantom limb pain of patients with amputations within a 24-month follow-up. Int J Rehabil Res 40:209-214
key_trials.finding: PLP reduced and maintained at 24 months; no change in controls (p<.001); purposive sampling

key_trials.citation: Nia NG et al. 2018. Comparing EMDR with guided imagery on pain severity in rheumatoid arthritis. J Pain Res 11:2107-2113
key_trials.design: 3-arm controlled trial; self-described RCT, but participants were selected non-randomly
key_trials.finding: Both EMDR and guided imagery reduced pain vs control. The abstract's subscale means favour guided imagery, yet its conclusion favours EMDR. Shares an author (Behnammoghadam) with Rostaminejad 2017

key_trials.citation: Zat Ciftci Z et al. 2024. A randomized controlled trial of EMDR therapy in the treatment of fibromyalgia. Front Psychiatry 15:1286118
key_trials.design: RCT, TAU + 15 EMDR sessions vs TAU
key_trials.finding: EMDR improved VAS pain, WPI, SSS, depression, sleep and trauma symptoms through 3-month follow-up after Bonferroni correction. Proponent group (senior author Konuk). The abstract reports TSC-40 p=0.21 alongside a claim of significance

key_trials.citation: Cope SR et al. 2025. Randomised feasibility study evaluating EMDR for functional neurological disorder (MODIFI). J Neurol 272:493
key_trials.design: Randomised feasibility trial, EMDR + neuropsychiatric care vs care alone
key_trials.finding: Feasible (88% adherence); greater satisfaction, FND improvement and reductions in PTSD, depression, dissociation and disability; not powered for efficacy

key_trials.citation: Ramisch M et al. 2026. Personalized psychotherapy in IBS: pilot RCT (PIONEER-IBS). J Psychosom Res 211:113003
key_trials.design: Pilot RCT, personalised vs reverse allocation to EMDR or gut-directed hypnotherapy vs TAU
key_trials.finding: Feasible; no difference between personalised and reverse allocation; within-group somatic symptom improvement

key_trials.citation: Tesarz J et al. 2014. Effects of EMDR treatment in chronic pain patients: a systematic review. Pain Med 15:247-63
key_trials.design: Systematic review (2 controlled trials + 10 observational studies)
key_trials.finding: Large but heterogeneous pain reductions; no adverse events; insufficient evidence for recommendations

key_trials.citation: Singla A et al. 2025. EMDR for chronic pain: a systematic review. J Integr Complement Med 31:1045-1055
key_trials.finding: All studies reported pain improvement; effects large in 3 RCTs, moderate in 2, small or n.s. in 1; 'promising' but heterogeneous

controversy: The long-standing 'purple hat' critique (Davidson & Parker 2001; Lohr et al. 1999; Herbert, Lilienfeld et al. 2000, Clin Psychol Rev; Rosen; McNally) holds that the eye movements add nothing beyond exposure and that EMDR was marketed pseudoscientifically. Lee & Cuijpers (2013) and working-memory research partly rebut the claim that eye movements are inert. Still, the 2024 IPD meta-analysis found no advantage over other therapies. Shapiro's doctorate came from an unaccredited school. Training was proprietary and gatekept until 1995, and certification remains expensive. EMDRIA claims EMDR is 'highly effective' for chronic pain and addiction on thin evidence. Pain RCTs are small, TAU-controlled, proponent-run and sometimes poorly reported (Nia 2018 is non-randomly selected and internally inconsistent), with implausibly large effects in some studies (g=-6.87 in Tesarz 2014). There is a risk of destabilisation in complex or dissociative trauma without adequate preparation.

popularity.reach_estimate: About 5 million cumulative clients (order of magnitude). Basis: organisational claims of more than 100,000 trained clinicians and 'millions' treated, plus routine PTSD use in NHS, VA and European services. Pain-specific reach is far smaller, probably tens of thousands.
popularity.method_notes: The trajectory is anchored on founding milestones (1987 observation, 1989 papers, 1990 Institute, 1995 EMDRIA and the first textbook) and guideline endorsements (WHO 2013, NICE/ISTSS 2018). It also uses PubMed annual publication counts queried this session, which rose ~13-fold from 1995 to 2025, and the 2021 Prince Harry media spike. Reach comes from organisational claims (over 100,000 clinicians, 'millions' treated) and is discounted to ~5 million. Reddit r/EMDR size (37,694 members, July 2025) came from a Wayback capture; Google Trends was not retrieved (no public API, web search unavailable 2026-10-13). The trajectory after 2020 is a judgment based on the PubMed growth and media coverage.
